title: A language prior sampled from developer docs rates ordinary English as distinctive
claim: A word-frequency table built from developer documentation omits words that are common in speech but rare in technical writing — silently, reaches, remains, holds — so a retriever using it as an English prior treats them as distinctive terms. The weak-match caveat that exists to catch a hit resting only on ordinary words is then suppressed exactly when the query is nothing but ordinary words.
expectation: A measured frequency table damps ordinary English, so a match resting only on filler is labelled weak and the reader is warned before acting on it.
reality: The table covers 2,460 terms sampled from developer documentation. `silently`, `reaches` and `reach` are absent from it, so they score as distinctive. Asked about a CLI flag that npm was swallowing, the retriever returned a finding about headless Chromium and the proxy at 75% confidence with no caveat, matched on `silently, reaches, reach, before, never`. The third-ranked hit was correctly labelled weak; the top two were not.
mechanism: The caveat fires when no matched term is both informative and uncommon. Commonness is looked up in the measured table, so a word the table never sampled is treated as uncommon by default. A developer-documentation corpus systematically under-samples ordinary narrative English, which is precisely the vocabulary a person writes when describing a failure in their own words — so the gap in the table lines up exactly with the queries the caveat is meant to catch.
appliesTo: Any retriever using a domain-sampled frequency list as a general language prior, where absence from the list is read as evidence of rarity.
workaround: Read absence from a domain-sampled table as unknown rather than as rare. Either source the prior from a general English frequency list, or require positive evidence of rarity before counting a word as distinctive. A hand-maintained residual list does not close the gap: this project has forty such words and none of the three that caused the failure are among them.

evidence.command: node -e "const r=require('./data/word-frequency.json').rates; for (const w of ['silently','reaches','reach']) console.log(w, r[w])"
evidence.output:
silently undefined
reaches undefined
reach undefined
evidence.note: Ordinary English, absent from a 2,460-term developer-documentation sample.

evidence.command: node bin/cairn-find.js "npm run cairn:find -- --before is silently ignored, the flag never reaches the script"
evidence.output:
cairn-0013     7.6  Headless Chromium sends localhost through the proxy and times out silently
      confidence 75% [precondition holds here]
      matched: silently, reaches, reach, before, never
evidence.note: No weak-match caveat on a hit whose every matched term is ordinary English.

check.confirmedIf: prints missing=1 or more: ordinary English words are absent from the prior and will score as distinctive
check.refutedIf: prints missing=0: the prior covers ordinary narrative English

observations.note: Found by using the tool rather than evaluating it. Queried cairn with four real failures from this session; all four returned unrelated findings, and the two highest-scoring carried no caveat.
